messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate (us-east-1) — 5xx rate jumped from 0.8% to 27% in the last 3m. Error class: SIGSEGV / OOM in model-runner. Trigger: anomaly-detector v2. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/alerts/2539876543 :rotating_light:

Sam Nguyen: got it, I'm oncall. Paging eng-runtime and eng-sre. First check: are there any deploys in the last 10m?

Maya Chen: no deploys from prod pipeline in the last 30m. I see node churn on pool-gpu-3, logs show repeated segfaults from model-runner process.

Jordan Patel: copying logs —
```
[2026-03-15T18:02:12Z] model-runner[pid=4321]: allocate_kv_cache() -> oom at 0x7f9c3e...
[2026-03-15T18:02:13Z] model-runner[pid=4321]: SIGSEGV at 0x000000000000 (pc=0x7f9c4a...)
[2026-03-15T18:02:13Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4321 (model-runner) score 987
[2026-03-15T18:02:14Z] gpu0: thermal throttling? temp=84C
```

Luis Torres: thermal throttling + OOM + segfaults suggests a memory/driver regression or a bad quantized kernel. Any recent model quantization or kernel roll?

Maya Chen: we did push a new kernel selection patch to runtime-alpha yesterday, but that hasn't been promoted. This looks like a live instance on Dedicated fleet still using older runtime.

Sam Nguyen: immediate mitigation options we can do now:
- drain traffic from pool-gpu-3
- route traffic to model-variant: redwood/llama-13b-fallback (lower mem)
- reduce batch size and max_tokens at gateway for the route
- increase eviction threshold for KV cache

Jordan Patel: I'm doing drain: `kubectl label node pool-gpu-3 node.kubernetes.io/drain=true --overwrite` and cordon/evict problematic pods.

ops-bot: ACTION: node pool-gpu-3 cordon started by Jordan Patel at 2026-03-15T18:05:00Z

Jordan Patel: evicting now, will fallback to pool-gpu-1 and pool-gpu-2.

Support Bot: Customer impact check: endpoints affected — all traffic using model-id `redwood/llama-70b-prod` routed through pool-gpu-3. Current error rate on customers: 16 tenant IDs showing >=5% error increase. Listed: tenant-389, tenant-441, tenant-702, others.

Sam Nguyen: set temporary routing policy in gateway: `route: /v1/generate -> prefer: redwood/llama-70b-safefallback, fallback: redwood/llama-13b-fallback` and cap `max_tokens=512`, `batch_size=4` for next 20m.

Maya Chen: applying gateway change now. Patch: 
```yaml
- route: /v1/generate
  prefer_model: redwood/llama-70b-safefallback
  fallback_model: redwood/llama-13b-fallback
  overrides:
    max_tokens: 512
    batch_size: 4
    timeout_ms: 30000
```

Maya Chen: done. Requests are draining to safefallback pool. 5xx rate on /v1/generate dropped from 27% -> 5% over 2 mins.

Sam Nguyen: good. Initiate rolling restart for model-runner on pool-gpu-3 nodes after cordon/evict to clear state. Also increase alert sensitivity to watch for recurrence.

Luis Torres: I'll open a debug job to reproduce locally with the quant kernels and mem profile. Assigning to eng-runtime.

eng-runtime: picking this up. Immediate triage steps:
1) collect coredumps from crashed pods (`/var/crash`),
2) gather nvmem logs and driver versions (`nvidia-smi -q`),
3) capture model config + quantization metadata for affected runs.

Jordan Patel: coredumps collected: s3://redwood-crashlogs/2539876543/cores.tar.gz
Driver versions from node pool-gpu-3: 535.86.10, CUDA 12.1.

Maya Chen: note: some pods showed `driver API mismatch` before restart. Kernel backtrace points at `libgpu_kernels.so::quant_conv`

Sam Nguyen: customer comms — Support, please prepare a short note for tenants with high error rates. Use: "We detected an infrastructure-level issue causing elevated error rates. We've routed traffic to fallback models and mitigations are in place; we expect full recovery within 30 minutes. We'll follow up with root cause and any customer-specific request logs."

Support Bot: Drafted message and pinging account managers for tenants >10% error. Template posted to #support-urgent.

Maya Chen: rolling restart done on cordoned nodes, re-enabled pool with new label `isolated=true` for further observation. Memory usage per pod stabilized after restart.

ops-bot: NODE: pool-gpu-3 uncordon scheduled at 2026-03-15T18:28:00Z by Sam Nguyen

Sam Nguyen: handoff plan — I'm ending my oncall shift in 20m. Jordan, can you take primary for post-mortem coordination and RCA?

Jordan Patel: taking primary. I'll collate logs, link crash artifacts, and own the RCA. Initial hypothesis: GPU driver + quant kernel compatibility + memory leak under certain seq-lengths. Next steps: reproduce with stress harness, test with driver 535.86.10 vs 540.x, and run kv-cache eviction stress test.

Luis Torres: assigning a patch branch: `fix/quant-kernel-safety-2539876543` and will run CI with heavy quant conv tests.

Sam Nguyen: customer impact summary for handoff: ~16 tenants affected, peak error rate 27% on /v1/generate, mitigation applied (routing + batch caps) reduced errors to ~<6%, no data exfiltration, some requests truncated due to token cap.

Jordan Patel: noted. I'll schedule post-incident review for 2026-03-16 09:00 PT. Please add any timeline events to the incident doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/2539876543

Sam Nguyen: thumbs up. tagging Oncall Rotation for follow-up: @Oncall Rotation please confirm coverage for the 09:00 PT review. :thumbsup:

Oncall Rotation: Confirmed. We'll join.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: status changed to "Mitigated" by Sam Nguyen at 2026-03-15T18:30:00Z — follow-up required: RCA and driver/kernel fix.

Jordan Patel: capturing follow-ups:
- reproduce local crash and PR fix for quant kernel (eng-runtime)
- validate driver compatibility matrix and update deployment gating (eng-infra)
- add automated kv-cache eviction thresholds to prevent full OOM (eng-platform)
- update playbook with this thermal + OOM pattern (eng-oncall)

Sam Nguyen: thanks team. I'll close active paging. Jordan will take post-mortem ownership.

Jordan Patel: closing thread for now, will reopen if error rate creeps back up. Archiving logs and artifacts.
